column2: A hundredfold lower than him is Kali's wife, always known as Alakshmi; in the world she is remembered as Manthara.
Tenfold lower than her is Viprachitti, always; he is declared to be Jarasandha, and after him Kalanemi.
A hundredfold lower than him is the one famed as Kamsa; fivefold lower than him are the two called Madhu and Kaitabha.
Those two are to be known as Hamsa and Hidimbaka, O Janardana. Equal to Viprachitti is Bhauma, remembered on earth.
Eightfold lower than him is Hiranyakashipu; threefold lower than him is the great asura Hiranyaksha.
Manimat is to be known as his equal, and Baka as a little lower. Twentyfold lower than him is the great asura called Taraka.
Sixfold lower than him is Shambara, the thorn of the world; Shalva, lowest among the Daityas, is to be known as equal to Shambara.
Hidimba is said to be twofold lower than Shambara; lower still is Bana, known by the name Kichaka.
The one called Dvapara, Mahahasa, is remembered as equal to the asura Bana; tenfold lower than him is Namuchi, best of Daityas.
Paka and Ilvala are both to be known as equal to Namuchi; fourfold lower than him is Vatapi, lowest of Danavas.
One and a half times lower than him is the Daitya king named Dhenuka; half again lower than Dhenuka is the Daitya Keshi.
The great asura Trinavarta is to be known as equal to Keshi; tenfold lower than him is the one named Hamsa, O lord of Rama.
Tririka is to be known as his equal, and Pauruka likewise; he is to be known as Veta in a former birth, O good one.
Onefold lower than him are Kumbhandaka and Kuparnaka; Duhshasana is to be known as equal to Jarasandha, O Lord.
Vikarna, best of Daityas, is to be known as equal to Kamsa; a hundredfold lower than Kumbhakarna is the one famed as Kradhya.
A hundredfold lower than him is the great asura Shatadhanva; the best of Daityas, Karmari, is to be known as his equal.
Kalakeya is always held to be equal to Vena. The equality of the lower Daityas with the higher is spoken of
on account of possession, and so it should be understood of the gods too; there is no doubt. A hundredfold lower than him is the great asura Chittamani;
the one who presides over that body is a hundredfold higher than him. A hundredfold lower than him is the great asura Hastamani;
a hundredfold lower than him is the great asura Padamani; the one presiding over the sense of sight is a hundredfold higher than him.
The one presiding over the eye-sense is a hundredfold higher than him; a hundredfold lower than him is the great asura Sparshamani.
A hundredfold lower than him is the great asura Chandamani; a hundredfold lower than him is the great asura Shishnamani.
A hundredfold lower than him is the asura remembered as Karmamani. All the office-holders beginning with Rudra, impelled at the beginning of the kalpa and so on,
sometimes act very much against you, O good one; but Vayu and I never act against you.
In the original forms and partial incarnations of Rudra and the others, O great Lord, understanding is lost; therefore they are all called 'broken.'
But my understanding, O lord of the earth, is unbroken; therefore I am called 'unbroken.' Even so, O God, I have no power to praise you.
Show compassion to me, your devotee of unbroken devotion, O great Lord." Having praised Hari thus, Brahma stood before him with joined palms.
From the sense of taste he created Varuna, its presiding deity; and after twenty years the Lord, from that same sense,
Brahma created the Ganga, deity of the sense of taste, after Varuna, ten years later.
From his lap Brahma created Narada, dear to the Lord; and after Narada, sixty years later,
the Lord Brahma created Agni from the sense of touch; then, five years later, the presiding deity of speech.
Brahma created Svaha, whom they call the deity of mantras. After Agni, O lord of birds, he created Bhrigu, best of brahmin sages,
ten years later, from between his brows; and a year later he created Bhrigu's wife.
After Bhrigu, a hundred years later, the Lord Brahma himself begot Kashyapa from his mind.
A year later the Lord created Aditi; and after Kashyapa, ten years later, Atri.
After Atri, ten years later, Brahma begot Bharadvaja, and after him Vasishtha.
Ten years later, and a year apart in turn, the lotus-seated one created their wives.
After Vasishtha the Lord created Gautama, and ten years later he created Jamadagni.
Ten years later came Manu Vaivasvata; and after Manu, a hundred years later, was born
the fortunate Vishvaksena, son of Vayu, of great strength; fourteen years after him came the lord of the Ganas.
Born after him, O lord of birds, eight years later, came the lord of wealth, and his wife in the following year.
After Vishvaksena, ten years later, the lotus-seated one created Jaya and the other devotees of the Lord.
After Jaya and the others Brahma created the deities of action, Valla and the rest; and a hundred years later he created Shiva's mount.
After the deities of action, thirty years later, Brahma created Parjanya, presiding deity of mantras and yantras.
After Parjanya, ten years later, Brahma begot Pushkara, presiding deity of the principle of action.
Thus did Brahma create by my grace, O lord of birds; knowing this one attains liberation, and not otherwise in any way.
The essence of pepper, the essence of cumin, the essence of oblations cooked in ghee, the essence of what is cooked and fried in oils, the essence of jaggery, the essence of butter,
the essence of cloves and the essence of sugar — such essences Vasudeva enjoys. Lakshmi's lord, abode of the whole world, and at his command Vasudeva too, always.

Hear, best of disciples, of the portions of the remaining essences enjoyed by the lord of the earth, the great soul. Thus bewildered are Vasudeva's devotees — what need be said of Vishnu's devotees in the world?
They are blessed, enjoyers of the essence alone, and for them sorrow does not increase. Know those who eat while omitting the Vaishvadeva offering to be wicked and intent only on eating.

I will tell you something special about the Vaishvadeva, lord of birds, secret, which the learned do not tell elsewhere: those who give to the sun and the others without Vayu and Hari dwelling within —
they are always to be known as eaters of the mere essence; therefore Vishnu alone is the great Self. He enjoys the portion of essence, not everything; with unobstructed power he enjoys all.

I will tell you again of other essences, lord of birds; hear this secret with great attention. Grapes and the like, all things spoiled by time and the like or spoiled in their nature, are without essence.
After becoming over-ripe, and likewise after four days, they are to be known as without essence and impure; so too the jambu fruit is remembered.
After a month, O lord of birds, the jackfruit is held to be without essence; after six months, O lord of birds, the date is remembered as bitter.
A fresh, pure coconut, once broken open, O Lord, is declared to be without essence after a day and a night.
A dried coconut and dates likewise; the mango is declared to be without essence after a fortnight.
The areca nut is declared so after a year, O lord of birds, and betel after a ghatika.
Cooked rice, rice with dal, milk-rice, snacks and boiled things are declared to be without essence after one watch, O lord of birds.
What is cooked in oil is so remembered after three fortnights, O lord of birds, and what is cooked in ghee after four watches.
Vegetables are declared without essence after three watches; citron, ginger, amla, camphor and mango
are declared without essence after a year, O lord of birds; parpata is declared without essence after only a fortnight.
Tulasi is always full of essence, even on Ekadashi, O brahmin; whether fresh or dried, fresh tulasi is remembered as having essence.
On Ekadashi the wise should take tulasi, full of essence, by the skin and the nose, but not by the tongue.
On Ekadashi Hari's food is declared to be without essence; on Ekadashi Hari's holy water, for men, O lord of birds,
is full of essence once and more so twice; on Ekadashi, O fortunate one, holy water mixed with perfumes and the like
is declared to be without essence, and likewise when mixed with sweet water. On Ekadashi Hari's milk, ghee and honey-water
are without essence for lords of men — this is the view of the knowers of the Veda. In the month of Ashadha, O Garuda, vegetables are said to be without essence;
in the month of Bhadrapada, O lord of birds, curd is said to be without essence; and milk in the month of Ashvina is declared without essence.
A woman without the upright mark and the mace mark is sung of as without essence; those without devotion to Hari are declared to be asuras.
A mouth without Hari's name is called without essence; cooking without an offering to Hari is called without essence.
The flax flower is declared without essence after three days; jasmine (mallika) keeps its essence for a watch, and jati jasmine for half a watch;
the hundred-petalled lotus for three watches, the oleander for a day and a night, and the parijata keeps its essence for a ghatika, O lord of birds.
Saffron is said by the wise to keep its essence for three years, musk for ten years, and camphor for a year;
sandal is declared always full of essence. Now hear, lord of birds, I will tell of the things that are pure yet without essence:
husks, sacrificial fuel, sour rice-water, punyaka, bhissata, upodvraji, the bottle gourd, the large ridge gourd,
brinjal, sorrel, bilva and udumbara, onion, garlic, stalks and kalanja, O brahmins —
all these are declared without essence at all times. On Ekadashi the Vaishvadeva, shraddha and libations,
and cremating the dead with mantras, are declared without essence. The god Narayana, the offering itself, these inauspicious flavours
does not accept, does not accept, does not accept — Hari himself; yet he knows everything of beings who do evil.
Hari makes them taste, but does not himself taste. The eating of what lacks essence is the fruit of beings' karma.
Beings are eaters of what is secondary; Kunti and the others are eaters of what is primary. Vishnu drinks what is auspicious; the Lord does not drink the inauspicious.
Who can describe his activity? Hari himself is full bliss; there is no one like him in any place or time. I will tell of his incarnations; hear, best lord of birds.
Then Hari became Krishna, born to Devaki from Vasudeva — Vishnu himself — wishing to destroy Kamsa and the others utterly and to protect the Pandavas well, O lord of birds.
Then, when Kali had begun, Hari, to delude the asuras, O lord of birds, was born among the Kikatas by the name of Buddha, only to set aside the authority of the Veda.
Then Hari, called Kalki, O lord of birds, will arise at the junction between the ages, in the house of Vishnugupta, to slay the kings who have become little better than robbers.
Keshava and the rest are twenty-four; Sankarshana and the others; Vishva and the others a thousand; and those beginning with Para are held to be countless.
The incarnations of Vishnu Narayana are countless; each of them is Narayana himself, not differing by even an atom
in strength, form or qualities in any way. Infinite, with infinite qualities, Vishnu is full, and not otherwise.
He always shows Hari directly to those fit for liberation at the proper time; therefore he is called Prajna (wisdom).
He always shows Hari to all, even indirectly; therefore Vayu, O lord of birds, is always declared to be Knowledge.
Because he teaches what is good and bad, dwelling in the hearts of devotees, that Maruta also received the name Guru.
Dwelling in the hearts of yogis, he meditates on the supreme Hari; meditating on him even as distinct, he is remembered as the Great Meditator.
He knows the supreme Hari according to his worthiness, and always knows the qualities present in Rudra and the others;
therefore he is called Vijna (the discerning one), O best of birds. Because of giving up actions done from desire, he is remembered as Viraga.
Or, dwelling always in the hearts of yogis, that Maruta produces detachment; so he is remembered as Viraga.
Through the merit and sin of the gods there is only happiness, increasing higher and higher, and that happiness belongs to the higher ones up to Vayu.
Since Vayu produces a share of happiness for gods, sages and excellent men, he is called Sukha (happiness).
He always enjoys it, O lord of birds, and there Maruta is chief. If any sorrow, grief and the like arises for the gods, O Lord,
know that it is due to possession by asuras; there is no doubt. It belongs to that being, and arises in turn for the Daityas.
Since Kali is the greatest [in sorrow], he is remembered as the sorrowful one. Through the merit and sin of the Daityas there is only sorrow, increasing higher and higher,
and that sorrow belongs to the higher ones up to Kali; he always enjoys it, O lord of birds, and so he is remembered as Kali.
If any happiness, joy and the like arises for the Daityas, O Lord, it is due to possession by the gods; there is no need to consider this.
For the gods there is no hell, O son of Vinata; and for the Daityas there is no happiness in their nature, not even that arising from sense objects, O brahmin.
Whatever arises from sense objects is declared to be due to possession by the gods. For the gods there is no tamas at all, and no sorrow in their nature.
Great sorrow arising from sense objects never exists for the gods; any sorrow, grief and the like would come from possession by asuras.
So Kali is always sorrowful and Vayu always happy. For men and sages, O lord of birds, happiness and sorrow
arise from their merit and sin, and Maruta enjoys merit. Breaker of suffering, destroyer of Kali — there is no need to consider this.
From Prana to Sukha there are nineteen portions; they have entered the worlds and exist separately, O lord of birds.
Hear, best lord of birds, of Maruta's incarnations. Among the fourteen Indras, the second, Virochana,
is declared to be Vayu, O lord of birds, among Indra and the others; he is the all-pervading one whose eye rests on all the principles of Hari.
Therefore he, a portion of the Maruts, is proclaimed by the name Rochana. In the Rama incarnation Hanuman accomplished Rama's purpose; he himself was born on earth as the mighty Bhimasena.
In the Krishna incarnation he is to be known as the declared portion of the Maruts.
A Daitya named Manimat will be called Sankara; he will surely bring about the mixing (sankara) of all.
So he will bear the name Sankara, O lord of birds, and will utterly destroy all the Bhagavata dharmas.
Then Vasudeva will surely appear on earth, one whose equal in the aims of sacrifice does not exist in the fourteen worlds.
So he will surely be full of wisdom. Vayu has three incarnations, and the doctrine called Bhagavata.
Establishing it and subduing the wicked are the only two purposes; Vayu has no other purpose, nor in the form of Vairochana.
In the three incarnations, O lord of birds, the sorrow arising from the womb and the like does not exist for Vayu at all, nor in Vairochana and the rest.
In the four incarnations there is no connection with semen and blood, none at all, O lord of birds, and so nothing inauspicious.
First drying up the womb, at the time of birth the Lord of gods appears in the four incarnations.
The twenty-three forms of Vayu, O lord of birds, with the forms of the straight nature of Brahma, the Supreme One,
are truly, without doubt, in eternal bliss and happiness; so one should understand, and not otherwise in any way.
By merely hearing this they attain liberation, without doubt. Now I will tell of those born after them; hear, best lord of birds.
From Krita and Pradyumna, O lord of birds, two women were born as twins, and of the two, the one who was superior
is known as Vani, O lord of birds, and also as Brahmani. She is held to be Savitri, wife of Viranchi called Purusha; as wife of the four-faced one she is proclaimed Sarasvati.
Thus Vani is to be known as threefold, O best of birds. Now I will tell of the incarnations of Bharati; hear with a collected mind.
Because she presides over all the Vedas she is remembered as having all the Vedas as her self; she is proclaimed the wife of Vayu, the Great Meditator.
She is proclaimed the wife of Vayu, whose form is knowledge. Because her nature is always happiness, Bharati is of the nature of happiness;
she is proclaimed the wife of Vayu, whose nature is happiness. Vayu himself is called the Guru, and she is devoted to him;
therefore the eternal Bharati is remembered as devotion to the Guru; she is proclaimed the wife of Vayu, the great Guru.
Because she is full of love for Hari, she is remembered as Hariprit; she is proclaimed the wife of Vayu, whose form is steadfastness.
Because she presides over all mantras, she is remembered as having all mantras as her self; she is proclaimed the wife of Vayu, the great Lord.
All enjoyments are enjoyed only for Vishnu's pleasure; so Bharati is to be known and proclaimed by the name Bhuji.
She is proclaimed the wife of Vayu of wondrous form; the wife of Rochana-Indra is proclaimed by the name Shraddha.
Then Hanuman was born in the Treta age, O best of birds; then from a brahmin named Shiva was born she who is remembered as Bharati.
Not Bharati alone, but joined with Shachi and the others; all who were born in her attained union with their own husbands.
The maiden called Tanmati is to be known as 'one who went to another.' At the end of the Treta, O lord of birds, she herself, joined with Shachi and the others,
was born of Damayanti and Nala and is called Indrasena; because she delighted Nala she is called Nalanandini.
There she did not attain union with her own husband, O lord of birds; there her 'going to another' is to be understood as through Vayu dwelling in a man.
After staying thus for some time, she died a maiden. She herself, joined with Shachi and the others, [was born] of the great-souled Drupada,
arising from the middle of the altar for the sake of Bhimasena; there there was no 'going to another,' and she was united with her husbands.
Bharati alone is to be known as the daughter of the king of Kashi; she is to be known by the name Kali, ever dear to Bhimasena.
Draupadi, daughter of Drupada, was joined with Vach and the others. Giving up her body, she alone remaining, in the village called Karati,
she will be born in the house of Sankara in the Kali age, O lord of birds; for the sake of Vayu's third form, that maiden died.
These and others are the wives of Vayu and the wives of Brahma, O good one; and they are a hundredfold lower than their own husbands in qualities, O lord of birds.
Addressed thus by them, and saying "So be it," O best of brahmins, she, joined with Parvati and the others, became Bharati on earth.
In the house of a brahmin named Shiva, that maiden performed austerities for the sake of union in action with Vishnu, who bore the name Shiva.
Pleased by her austerity, Vishnu, the great Lord called Shiva, gave a boon: "In this third, the Krishna birth, O women,
there will be proper union with your own husbands, apart from Bhava; since by her, by Parvati, you were all impelled,
she showed her dalliance to Brahma, the Supreme One; therefore that Parvati is foremost in Brahma's body, without doubt.
Even in Krishna's body there will be no union with her; in this second one there will surely be 'going to another.'"
Hari, dwelling within Rudra, having given the boon to the woman, vanished, and the glorious Lord went to his own world.
Giving up that body, they became daughters of Nala; taking the name Indrasena, they went to a grove of austerity.
Wandering there, they saw the sage Mudgala; at the mere sight of him they became infatuated with desire.
Destroying Mudgala's sense of self, Maruta enjoyed there the excellent women, Bharati and the others.
Released from that body, she became Draupadi; because she was born of Drupada she is remembered as Draupadi.
Because she arose from the middle of the altar she is remembered as not womb-born; because she was dark in colour she is remembered on earth as Krishna.
In Krishna's body too Bharati's presiding sense is always remembered; that of Shachi and the others only sometimes in that body.
At the time of union with her own husband, O best of birds, the presiding sense belongs to her alone, and not otherwise.
At the time of their enjoyment, O best of birds, Uma has no presiding sense at all; she is always in sleep alone.
At the time of Partha's enjoyment, in Draupadi's body, the twofold presiding sense of Bharati and Shachi is remembered.
Then the presiding sense of Uma and Shyamala is lost; for all of them there is only sleep; there is no need to consider this.
Vayu alone, having entered Arjuna in the form of a hero, always enjoys Bharati, and Yudhishthira Shyamala.
Maruta, having entered Nakula in a beautiful form, always enjoys Bharati, and Nakula Usha, O bird.
Maruta, having entered Sahadeva in the form of good conduct, always enjoys Draupadi, and Sahadeva Usha too, O bird.
Shachi and the others did not attain union with Maruta in Draupadi's body; therefore one should not think of their 'going to another' in Krishna's body.
Nor should one think of Bharati's union with the bodies of Dharma and the others; one should think of their union as with a human body.
For those who have direct realization there is no taint at all; or, as at Mudgala's time of love, O lord of birds,
they took their pleasure thus, and so there is no fault. On one day, O lord of birds, Dharma and Vayu both
enjoyed her fully in Krishna's body, O giver of honour; still, her not going to another is to be thought of, without doubt.
The gods know the enjoyment of gods and of what gods enjoy; they do not know mortals, nor themselves in those bodies again.

Only the swan knows how to separate milk from water, and no other; so one should think of union with her own husband through Krishna's body; 'going to another' in Krishna's body is not to be thought of, O lord of birds.

I have seen in your belly, O Lord, the three worlds and the destroyer of worldly existence, the conch, discus and the rest; how shall I see again and again such a belly of yours, O lord of Rama? — so he wept.

Full of bliss, full of nails, full of fine hair, full of down, full of virtues, full of a fine nose — your chest, O Lord, is broad, well adorned, shining with the stainless Kaustubha and with Lakshmi,
garudpurana:306:54	most tender, with the fine tulasi, well flowered and anointed with sandal — such a chest of yours I have seen through your compassionate glance.
garudpurana:306:55	How may I see it again and again? — so Rudra wept with devotion. Therefore Rudra received the name Uru, and his son was the one called Daurva — he himself.
Because he wept and made it wide (urvarita), Rudra came to be called Aurva. Aurva, seeing people fit for liberation yet utterly fixed on sense objects,
praised the lotus feet of Vishnu, and remembering them again and again, his throat was choked. "Those most sinful ones, serving sinful things, day after day enjoy vile objects with vile senses;
when will they give these up with the understanding that they are to be rejected? I do not know" — so he wept deeply. "These fools strive with great eagerness to obtain objects of desire;
for the sake of vile senses they give up wealth and the like, all fixed on sense objects. When will you release these, deluded by your maya, their understanding lost, O form of the universe?"
Remembering again and again Vasudeva's maya, Aurva wept, his limbs trembling with fear. "With great hardship, through worldly occupations, they resort to wretchedness, abandoning their own true work;
with great wretchedness all these sinners gather wealth and the like, and all, like beasts, throw away in vain the goods and wealth earned with hardship.
Through Murari's maya they never give it to a worthy recipient with the understanding that he is Vishnu. The great say their life is wasted; how are they lost?" — so he wept deeply.
So, lord of birds, know Aurva, in the form of Rudra, as one always well instructed by Krishna. When Sati, Daksha's daughter, lord of birds, gave up her body at Daksha's sacrifice
and was born again of Menaka to Himadri, then Rudra received the name Aurva. Saying, 'Be one whose seed goes upward,' he became one whose seed goes upward.
When the great god Rudra took the hand of the mountain's daughter, he became exceedingly devoted to her; so Rudra received the name Para.
Sadashiva and the others are the ten brothers of Rudra, and the three sons of Sumitra and Rohini; these are equal at the time of liberation and on the path, and a hundredfold lower than those two.
Garuda said: "Tell me the determination of bliss, O Krishna, ocean of full compassion, so that the wise may determine it, and to make it known to me.
Tell it to your disciple out of compassion, to lift me up always; you whose desires are fulfilled, O Krishna, what longing do you have, O Lord?"
Addressed thus by the great-souled lord of birds, Hrishikesha, the lotus-eyed Krishna, pleased, spoke with compassion.
Shri Krishna said: "Gayatri has a hundredfold bliss; the Creator has single bliss; such a hundredfold bliss is proclaimed for Brahma.
Shesha and the others have a hundredfold bliss, and Sarasvati, O best of birds; single bliss is to be known for Bharati, O son of Vinata.
Thus is the determination of bliss always to be known, O bird. Thus I have told you everything; what else do you wish to hear?"
At the great tirtha called Kapila she climbed the great mountain; seeing Shrinivasa dwelling there and bowing to him, the great, virtuous woman
fasted for three days, then went to Papavinashana; having bathed there, she went to a solitary place for the sake of marriage.
To its north, two krosha away, in a deep, hollow, solitary place, she performed excellent austerity.
Meditating on the god Narayana, the maiden stayed there; at the end of a thousand divine years she began to praise him.
The maiden said: "You alone are my mother and father, you alone my husband and friend; you alone my son and most venerable teacher, my friend, my sister and my beloved.
Even examining my beginningless and endless births, O Lord, I do not know; all these, father and the rest, are merely instrumental causes, but you are not merely instrumental.
So, Murari, let me be your wife alone — this then is my vow. No success comes from mere association with the wicked, O form of generosity.

O God, cut off the sight of those who revile you and mock your best servants; O Vishnu, cut off the sight of those who betray the teacher; O Krishna, cut off friendship with those who betray devotees;
O God, cut off speech with those hostile to you, and grant me union with your lotus feet. Salutations again and again to you who dwell on Shrishaila; salutations again and again to you, Shrinivasa.

O master, highest and lowest, lord of Rama, form of the first cause, a great time has passed without the sight of you; the sight of you, four-armed one, comes through means gathered over endless births.
How may I, beset with all faults, have your sight, O Lord? Be gracious to me, a servant of your servants, fit to be a servant, O Lord of gods, abode of the world."
Praised thus, Vishnu Shrinivasa, ocean of compassion, Janardana, king of boon-givers, appeared through her devotion.
Choose a boon; blessings on you; I, the giver of boons, have come here. Hearing the words spoken by Hari, she said with a smiling face,
speaking with supreme devotion to Shrinivasa, Lord of the world: "Let me be your wife, O beautiful Madhava."
Hearing her words, Shrinivasa spoke: the Blessed Lord said, "O fortunate maiden, in the Krishna birth on earth
I will be your husband; there is no need to consider this." Addressed thus, the maiden spoke to Hari, supreme mass of merit,
with great joy and a voice choked with delight. The maiden said: "In the Krishna birth let me be your wife on the first day;
let me be chosen first of the women through the rite." Told "Om," Madhusudana spoke again.
The Blessed Lord said: "Because you were held by the maiden and given by me, O passionate one, their heart's desires will surely be fulfilled."
Having given her this boon, he vanished right there; and the maiden, giving up her body there,
was born in the house of Kumbhaka, remembered by the name Nila. Kumbhaka, O fortunate one, was the brother-in-law of Nandashobha;
he is to be known as Kalpavaha, remembered as first of the ancestors. Going to the house of him who dwelt on Vrishabhachala, [I won her,] who was invincible through Shiva's boon, O best of birds.
Slaying the sons of Diti, I obtained Nila, O lord of birds. Then the maiden was born in the house of King Nagnajit.
Nagnajit was Kavyavaha, and the maiden was named Nila. At her svayamvara, the seven bulls,
which through Shiva's boon could not be slain by gods or men — binding the bulls and defeating the kings, I won Nila, O great bird.
Nila, Kumbhaka's daughter, and those dwelling in her body strongly entered; since they were of one body, she entered there itself.
She was born on earth in two forms, a maiden, without doubt. Now I will tell of Bhadra's birth; hear, best lord of birds.

In the village where the Bhagavata scripture is not present, nor Bhagavatas who relish it; in the house where the essence of the Gita's meaning is absent, or in the village where the Thousand Names is absent,
garudpurana:308:30	where there are none who relish those two — there one should not dwell even for a moment in any way. The day on which there is no divine story of Vishnu, that creature's life is wasted.
garudpurana:308:31	There is no need to consider this once one has gone to the womb; it is thought rare in the world of mortals. An ear adorned with ornaments and beautiful is not beautiful, say the noble connoisseurs;
garudpurana:308:32	only the ear adorned with the ornaments of Vishnu's stories do the noble call beautiful. So those who always hear the essence of the meaning of the Bhagavata and constantly recite it —
garudpurana:308:33	the great call their birth well-founded, and great is their fruit. Those mortals too who hear or always recite Hari's story wearing turban and jacket
garudpurana:308:34	are all to be honoured in the world, not those attached to sex and belly. Those who, out of obligingness or greed for wealth, always recite the Purana, the essence of the truth of the Lord,
garudpurana:308:35	and those who conceal the secrets of the truth — their destination is always the son of the Sun (Yama). Those who always generate a taste for the section on dharma and the section on rites,
garudpurana:308:36	and those who tell the Purana for a price — their destination is always the son of the Sun. Those who hear the Bhagavata Purana, the essence of the meaning of Hari's scripture, for a price,
garudpurana:308:37	and those who perform Vedic study for a price — their destination is always the son of the Sun. Those content with wealth that comes by chance are always fit for this;
garudpurana:308:38	those possessed by excessive thirst for earning wealth have no entitlement to the Bhagavata. Thinking always that in the world Hari alone is the inner controller and there is no Lord other than him —
garudpurana:308:39	those who always reflect thus, Vishnu bears their welfare and security. For good Vaishnavas there is no misfortune at all; it only appears so through knowledge mixed with doubt.
garudpurana:308:40	Hari gives the fruit of good and bad according to karma; so one should not strive for that, for wealth, but should strive in the truth of Hari.
garudpurana:308:41	So, having bathed, recited the divine mantra, and removed the scent of Vishnu's used offerings, becoming pure, one who knows all should always have the Bhagavata Purana recited.
garudpurana:308:42	Earning wealth according to karma, gaining the Vedas and gaining the scriptures will come, and hearing too; but hearing of Vishnu with great eagerness is hard to achieve.
garudpurana:308:43	To relish with great eagerness the essence of the Bhagavata is hard in the world of mortals; having relished the Bhagavata Purana, to be filled with tears of bliss is hard;
garudpurana:308:44	having heard, to hold the determination of the principles is all very hard, say the noble; and after holding the principles, to digest desire and anger is hard;
garudpurana:308:45	after hearing and holding the principles, union in yoga is likewise hard;
garudpurana:308:46	after hearing and holding the principles, digesting desire and anger is hard. These faults always make even those purified by knowledge full of doubt here.
garudpurana:308:47	So I shall always listen to good stories; there is nothing to consider here. With this resolve, longing for Hari's name, she set her mind on hearing; hearing thus until her body ended, she gave up her body and was born on earth
to dwell in the womb of Vasudeva's sister, O bird; born of the one named Sumitra, she was Mitravinda.
Through hearing she gained Hari as her friend (mitra); so she came to be called Mitravinda.
At the svayamvara, amid the kings, the passionate Mitravinda placed the garland on my shoulder; taking her, O lord of birds, and scattering all the kings, we reached the city, O lord of birds.

The goods made for friends and others went in vain and became like filth; the goods made for good Vaishnavas always become a means to attaining Hari.
garudpurana:309:21	Such has it been, Mukunda — enough, enough of the sorrow suffered through it. You always grant the company of the good; without you comes the company of the wicked.
garudpurana:309:22	Through constant company with the wicked, Murari, my body has burned without detachment. To what state shall such as I go, Mukunda? I do not know; protect me with compassion.
Such remorse, lord of birds, is the expiation, not shaving and the like. The Sun's daughter, having felt remorse, reflected on the true principle of Hari:

Hari alone is always highest of all, since he is full of all qualities; since in creation the whole universe arises from him, Hari is full of all qualities.
garudpurana:309:25	He is the first of the gods, the letter A itself, since Brahma and all the others are not full. Through Lakshmi's grace and long merit, Viranchi was born full of qualities according to his worthiness.
garudpurana:309:26	Viranchi is not full of qualities like Lakshmi, nor is Rama full of qualities like Vishnu; nor is Bharati full like Vayu, nor Varuni full like Shesha,
garudpurana:309:27	nor is Parvati full in form like Rudra; and so the others too are never full. Having reflected thus, she performed austerity on the bank of the Yamuna.
At that time I went to the bank of the Yamuna with Partha for hunting, O bird; seeing her there performing austerity, I said to my friend Partha:
O Partha, go quickly to the maiden and ask why she performs austerity here. Told thus, he went to her, asked the reason, and quickly
Phalguna returned and told me the whole story. Then at an auspicious moment I duly took her hand there.
Because of her constant ardour and her reflection on me, I am always pleased, well pleased; but for me, always rejoicing in full bliss, what happiness could come from her, lord of birds?
I accepted marriage with her only to show her grace, not for my happiness, O lord of birds. Now I will tell of Lakshmana's form and the reason for taking her hand, O lord of birds.
Hear it; I will tell you this secret; for a good disciple, nothing is secret to the teacher.
What is considered a lack of marks in him should not be thought of as bad marks. The twenty-eight marks of Hara should not be thought of like Bharati's, O lord of birds.
So Hara is always of the form of anger, because of the absence of those two; this was said truly. So those two are not in Rudra, O lord of birds; in sex and belly there is some excess.
Lakshmana and his other wives are endowed with twenty-seven marks; Varuni and the others with twenty-six, and the moon with twenty-five;
Artha is endowed with twenty-four; Nasatya and Vayu with twenty-two; and Shachi, without doubt, with twenty-one marks.
Pravaha is endowed with twenty, Yama with nineteen, Pashi with eighteen, and Anala with seventeen;
Vaivasvata with sixteen, Mitra with fifteen, the lord of wealth with fourteen, and Pavaka with thirteen;
the Ganga is endowed with twelve, Budha with eleven, Shani with ten, and Pushkara with nine.
Then my sixteen thousand beloved wives are endowed with eight, and the ancestors with seven;
the divine Gandharvas with six, those after them with five; the kings of the earth are declared to have four, and others three.
A slight excess in the belly, shortness in the feet and ears, excess in the topknot — apart from these, O brahmin, in Shiva's wife too;
in Lakshmana five faults, apart from head, ankles and the like; with excess at the navel, there are eight faults in Ativahika;
with excess in the shanks, eight faults are always remembered for Shachi. So too faults are to be inferred, O lord of birds.
By hearing of bad marks, O lord of birds, one always becomes a knower of the truth. Big-bellied, with sagging navel, with slightly protruding fierce fangs,
eyes deep as a blind well, long ears, lips and nose, long ankles, crooked feet, bad nails and dark teeth,
long shanks and long penis, one testicle and one nostril, red beard, red body hair, and crooked mouth — so he is described;
like a burnt mountain, with a red back — this is remembered as Kali; hairless shoulders, hairless head, red cheeks and jowls,
always pale on the forehead, and on the left shoulder and hand, O bird; with a cruel glance, a squint, and a rasping voice,
gluttonous and a heavy drinker, his breasts like dried fruits, with hair on the thighs like new shoots, and likewise on the back and head;
on the forehead three long lines, two of them even, are declared; the fish mark shaped like a serpent is declared on his penis,
a fish shaped like a sandal is declared at the tip of the tongue, and the fish shaped like a penis is ascribed to his anus.
